1.31 Prove a backup holds every photo before deleting it

Symptom. A source tree, such as /Volumes/Archive/Photos, should already be held by a backup, such as /Volumes/Backup/Photos, and you want to free the source. The backup was made over years: folders moved, files were renamed, re-dated or rewritten with new metadata, so a path-by-path comparison reports thousands of differences that may or may not matter.

Prerequisites. Both trees are mounted and stable for the duration of the run; nothing imports, converts or edits into either. Install the indexer from phindex and dngc from DNG Compare; those books own their installation, options and archive layout. Choose an archive directory that is not on the source you mean to delete. Know which Lightroom catalog references the source, because deleting it makes those photos missing in that catalog.

Mechanism. Index both trees, so that every file has its identities: SHA-256, DNG raw blocks, image data, Lightroom’s fingerprint and a metadata record.

phindex --db source.sqlite --root /Volumes/Archive/Photos --workers 8
phindex --db backup.sqlite --root /Volumes/Backup/Photos --workers 8

Then account for the source in the backup by content rather than by name. phindex align groups files into units (a raw with its JPEG and sidecar), matches each unit by its strongest shared identity, and flags moved, renamed and split units. Units with no counterpart are reported as left-only; files not yet read as not-indexed.

phindex align --left source.sqlite --left-root /Volumes/Archive/Photos \
  --right backup.sqlite --right-root /Volumes/Backup/Photos --out align-report/

dngc run turns that accounting into a preserved, restorable record. With the indexes it pairs files through phindex align, settles unchanged pairs without reading them, and keeps every source file in one of three forms: identical to its backup counterpart, a verified delta against that counterpart, or a full copy when the backup has none. --metadata phindex takes metadata from the indexes and writes a searchable metadata section.

dngc run /Volumes/Archive/Photos /Volumes/Backup/Photos /Volumes/Backup/source-proof \
  --index source.sqlite backup.sqlite --metadata phindex
dngc verify /Volumes/Backup/source-proof --restore-sample 50

Equal raw pixels are not permission to delete. Two files with the same raw image can differ in the DNG wrapper, embedded previews, XMP, ratings, keywords and develop history; the source copy may carry the only record of edits made after the backup. That is why the archive keeps a delta for every pair whose bytes differ, instead of declaring the pair equivalent and dropping the difference.

Verify. Read align-report/summary.json and account for every left-only and not-indexed unit: each must either be preserved as a full copy by the run or be deliberately excluded with a reason. Require dngc verify to exit 0; it checks the byte records, deltas and originals, the metadata index and that the comparison finished, and --restore-sample N restores N records at random and checks their SHA-256. While the source still exists, restore a few files of your own choosing, including a renamed one and one with a metadata difference, with dngc restore ARCHIVE RELATIVE_PATH OUTPUT, and compare each with the source file byte for byte. Only then delete, and settle the source in Lightroom’s terms: relink the catalog’s photos to the backup through Lightroom (Repair locations) or accept that the catalog will show them as missing.

Undo. Nothing above writes to the source or the backup tree; the indexes and the archive are new files. After deletion, dngc restore ARCHIVE RELATIVE_PATH OUTPUT rebuilds any source file byte for byte, and dngc versions lists the contents a path has had.

Limits. A delta is rebuilt against its backup file, so the archive and the backup tree are one unit: keep both, keep the backup’s files unedited, and keep a second copy of the archive on another device if the source was the only other copy. --metadata phindex records come from the exiftool-rs engine, a separate metadata identity from Perl ExifTool; never compare an archive made one way with one made the other. A random restore sample is evidence, not proof for every record. This cookbook links the owning books for their tests and qualification; it has no retained deletion control of its own, and the procedure says nothing about cloud copies, which Lightroom manages separately.
